statement: For every odd integer x ≥ 3, floor((x+2)^{3/2}) − floor(x^{3/2}) ≥ 3 floor(√x). Proof: (x+2)^{3/2} > x^{3/2}+3√x because (x+2)^3 − (x^{3/2}+3√x)^2 = 3x+8 > 0, hence the floor difference is at least floor(3√x) ≥ 3 floor(√x). At image scale Y = floor(x^{3/2}) the depth-1 working window is (2/3) Y^{1/3} ≤ (2/3)√x, so the gap exceeds that whole window (ratio → 9/2). Therefore the image V(I) of any odd window I is a 3√X-separated packing, not a consecutive interval, and interval Erdős–Turán cannot be applied to y = floor(x^{3/2}). Not a depth-2 mixing theorem, not C_L nonempty, not a Paper B edit, and not a halt theorem.
